data.segment_description:
(Studio: Charles Gibson)  A record day on the stock market reported; Dow Jones figures cited.  

(Studio: Betsy Stark)  The euphoric market after last week's despair in response to the global response to this financial crisis featured; details given about the rise in the stocks of companies like GM and MorganStanley, what European governments are doing to shore up banks and about the American rescue plan; scenes shown from the market floor.  [TRADER  Edward Jones CIO Alan SKRAINKA†, University of Chicago business school economist Raghuram RAJAN†- comment on the market response.]  [British Prime Minister Gordon BROWN†- says our action is unprecedented.]  Diagram shown of the process needed to restart frozen credit markets  [Harvard University professor Kenneth ROGOFF†- comments on the no-risk loaning.]  The need for investors to respond to whether the billions spent on the rescue will actually work as shown if banks start lending again noted.  

(Studio: Charles Gibson)  Report introduced.  

(New York: David Muir)  What is needed to get the global economy back on track examined.  [University of California at Berkeley professor Robert REICH†- says businesses cannot get credit, so additional money is helpful; asserts the problem is a crisis in trust.]  [Charles Schwab investment strategist Liz Ann SONDERS†- says confidence needs to be gotten in the banks.]

(Studio: Charles Gibson)  The standings of presidential candidates Senators Barack Obama and John McCain in the latest ABC News/"Washington Post" poll cited.   (Wilmington, North Carolina: Ron Claiborne)  The McCain campaign in Republican states featured; details given about his talk about issues, including the economy.  [McCAIN&nbsp- says he has been fighting for this country since he was 17; states America needs a fighter; asserts we have 22 days to go and we have been written off!]  The poll figures against the McCain attack strategy cited.  A "New York Times" commentary from Bill Kristol on the dysfunctional nature of the McCain campaign quoted.  [Political analyst Stuart ROTHENBERG†- says McCain needs some good news.]  McCain's new proposals on the economy noted.   (Toledo, Ohio: Jake Tapper)  Obama's campaign featured; details given about the elements of his rescue plan for the middle class.  [OBAMA&nbsp- says his plan is based on j-o-b-s; calls for a rescue plan for the middle class that will provide relief.]  Poll findings on the voter support for Obama's understanding of economic problems cited.  [Ohio voters nursing student Hannah KOVACHS‡, farmer Joe WURZELBACHER†- offer views on the economy.]   (Studio: Charles Gibson; Washington: George Stephanopoulos)  The McCain camp's hope the financial crisis will break, the fundamentals illustrated in the poll that the country wants change, how McCain is saddled with President Bush's record and the problems in the economy for McCain while Obama is viewed in the poll as the stronger leader discussed.
